Processing-controlled defect distributions cause persistent subdiffusion in physical beta-aluminas Processing modulates the spatial distribution of charge-compensating defects, and that distribution causally drives the persistent subdiffusive transport observed in physical beta- and beta-double-prime-aluminas. external causal transport from the paper's simulated defect configurations to physical specimens, not merely causal effects internal to the declared LAMMPS model

The public eSSE demo reproduces the LPSCl-II path-entropy estimate Using the pinned eSSE estimator, lag time, path cutoff, and public precomputed LPSCl-II discrete trajectories reproduces the four notebook path-entropies and a total within the paper-reported 415.72 plus or minus 6.02 J/mol/K interval. the compact public LPSCl-II discrete-trajectory demo at commit c3eed1993ddfd23cdb27ed8a8b04d19e99d5260a; raw-coordinate discretization and other materials are excluded

Strict single-descriptor interpretation of path entropy across materials Path entropy alone is sufficient to uniquely assess or predict ionic conductivity across diverse inorganic ionic conductors. a deliberately strict operational interpretation of the paper's statements that path entropy is a quantitatively robust and universal metric; it does not attribute an exact deterministic law to the authors

The public NASICON initializer yields distinct initial rate sums for two same-composition configurations At comp=0.2 (Na3.4Zr2Si2.4P0.6O12) and 573 K, a deterministic scan of all 50 public configurations finds 14 pairs within 0.25 meV in mean active-event barrier. The exploratory maximum-rate-ratio pair, structures 48 and 49, yields mean barriers of 317.094 and 316.886 meV and aggregate initial hopping rates of 3.987 and 2.676 times 10^15 per second, respectively. the pinned public 8x8x8 initial configurations, fitted cluster expansions, event catalogue, attempt frequency, and code at commit 69eb10b7c52ddd85e39ebeb882b2e4ea617e7770; stochastic trajectory evolution and conductivity are excluded

Mean migration barrier alone identifies aggregate initial hopping rate At fixed NASICON composition and temperature, a mean migration-barrier summary alone is sufficient to identify the aggregate initial hopping rate. a deliberately strict intermediate-target stress test motivated by common barrier-to-rate promotions; not a verbatim claim by Deng et al., whose full model retains event-level barrier heterogeneity and occupancy

Mean migration barrier alone identifies macroscopic ionic conductivity At fixed NASICON composition and temperature, the mean migration barrier alone is sufficient to identify long-time macroscopic ionic conductivity. a strict barrier-to-conductivity promotion stress test; not a verbatim claim by Deng et al., whose simulations explicitly retain dynamic occupancy, spatial event structure, and correlated ion motion

Linear full-cell EIS alone uniquely allocates electrode contributions Within the declared two-electrode additive model, a full-cell linear EIS observation uniquely identifies the separate positive- and negative-electrode contributions. the sum-versus-difference measurement structure described by the 2nd-NLEIS work; practical noise, broader circuit families, and general battery causality are outside the formal witness

Therefore, the information is insufficient to confirm sufficiency or uniqueness across the broad scope claimed.
